method: Focused secondary research and design-artifact analysis; primary participant research excluded by user instruction.

sources.title: Teaching critical thinking
sources.authors: N. G. Holmes, C. E. Wieman and D. A. Bonn
sources.locator: Main paper: introduction, instructional approach and results; historical-cohort description.
sources.finding: Introductory physics students practised comparing data and models, choosing improvements and reflecting; prompts were progressively removed. The authors report improved experimental reasoning, including later-course evidence.
sources.limit: One institution and historical cohorts, not random assignment. Does not establish the effect of this interface or transfer a learning-effect size to PARALLAX.
sources.implication: Design inference: compare retained conditions, ask for an evidence-based next investigation and evaluate independent reasoning.

sources.title: An epistemology and expectations survey about experimental physics: Development and initial results
sources.authors: B. M. Zwickl, T. Hirokawa, N. Finkelstein and H. J. Lewandowski
sources.locator: Abstract: paired perspectives and initial formative deployment in 45 classes at 20 institutions.
sources.finding: E-CLASS compares students' own views of experimental physics with their perceptions of professional practice and grading expectations.
sources.limit: Abstract read. This is not a navigation-usability instrument, and PARALLAX has not administered or validated E-CLASS.
sources.implication: Design inference: ask separately what students think the experiment teaches and what they believe earns marks.

sources.title: Confirming what we know: Understanding questionable research practices in intro physics labs
sources.authors: Martin M. Stein, Emily M. Smith and N. G. Holmes
sources.locator: Methods, analysis of student records, results and discussion.
sources.finding: Analysis of records from 107 groups at three institutions connects confirmation-oriented laboratory goals with questionable research practices.
sources.limit: Context-specific qualitative evidence. It does not establish dishonesty in this cohort or validate H12 about model confidence.
sources.implication: Design inference: retain failed attempts and revisions; prompt limitations and alternative explanations rather than a predetermined correct conclusion.

sources.title: Preparative pre-laboratory online resources for effectively managing cognitive load of engineering students
sources.authors: C. M. Rathnayaka et al. (full author list not verified)
sources.locator: Publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic snippets; full-page retrieval failed.
sources.finding: The indexed abstract describes preparative resources in engineering thermodynamics, with student and staff perspectives used to investigate cognitive load.
sources.limit: Full methods and results unavailable in this review. No sample size, causal claim or numerical improvement is relied on.
sources.implication: Tentative design inference: stage preparation around the task; test recall and relevance rather than treating a read checkbox as competence.

sources.title: Structure-based knowledge acquisition from electronic lab notebooks for research data provenance documentation
sources.authors: Max Schröder, Susanne Staehlke, Paul Groth, J. Barbara Nebe, Sascha Spors and Frank Krüger
sources.locator: PubMed abstract and figure captions; PMC full text presented an access challenge.
sources.finding: Structured notebook content is used to acquire provenance information; a biomedical laboratory proof of concept covers seven protocols for the automated approach.
sources.limit: Abstract and captions read. Not evidence of student usability, complete automatic metadata capture or this app's scientific validity.
sources.implication: Design inference: link the executed record to method, source, parameters and revision; distinguish a protocol template from what actually happened.

sources.title: CALM user guidelines and rules
sources.authors: University of Edinburgh · Confocal and Advanced Light Microscopy
sources.locator: Training and registration; bookings; data handling; reporting failures; equipment shutdown instructions.
sources.finding: This facility specifies training, equipment booking, fault reporting and data responsibilities. Its laser shutdown instructions depend on the next booking.
sources.limit: A microscopy facility's own policy, not PARALLAX's policy or instructions for our equipment. Local staff must approve local operating rules.
sources.implication: Design inference: preserve training/permission boundaries, give faults an owner and require asset-specific standby rules; avoid generic idle power-off.

sources.title: Light Microscopy Core: Make a booking
sources.authors: University of Edinburgh · School of Biological Sciences
sources.finding: The core requires training before access to its online equipment-booking system and uses PPMS for bookings.
sources.limit: An operational example from another discipline, not evidence about local students' current booking problems or a product comparison.
sources.implication: Design inference: preparation acknowledgement, equipment permission and a reservation are separate states.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.date: Recommendation; current linked edition accessed 3 October 2026
sources.locator: SC 1.4.10 Reflow, 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 4.1.3 Status Messages.
sources.finding: The recommendation defines testable web-accessibility criteria, including reflow, keyboard operation and programmatically determinable status messages.
sources.limit: A standard is not a certificate. These selected criteria are not the entire AA checklist, nor a physical-accessibility assessment.
sources.implication: Design inference: provide typed IDs and list alternatives, visible keyboard focus and announced recovery; assess all applicable AA criteria separately.

sources.title: Using CO2 monitors
sources.locator: What monitoring can tell you; monitor choice/placement; representative readings and recording.
sources.finding: CO2 monitoring can provide a broad indication of ventilation. Snapshot readings can mislead and cannot demonstrate safe levels.
sources.limit: UK guidance, not Indian legal compliance or a specification for this unsurveyed room. No numerical alarm threshold is imported.
sources.implication: Design inference: show measurement provenance, age and quality; require an approved sampling plan before using observations for operational decisions.

sources.title: LEAF — Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework
sources.locator: Framework description, resource categories and pilot context.
sources.finding: LEAF addresses laboratory resource use through practical actions spanning energy, equipment, procurement and waste.
sources.limit: A programme framework, not a measured baseline for this lab. Its pilot savings do not establish our savings or certification.
sources.implication: Design inference: maintain a baseline, an owner and an evidence-backed action ledger; include repair and procurement alongside standby modelling.

sources.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
sources.authors: Hamsa Bastani, Osbert Bastani, Alp Sungu, Haosen Ge, Özge Kabakcı and Rei Mariman
sources.locator: Abstract, significance and experimental design. Linked correction body could not be retrieved.
sources.finding: The high-school mathematics trial contrasts unrestricted assistance with a teacher-guided tutor. Its reported outcomes distinguish supported practice from later unassisted performance.
sources.limit: Different age, subject and task. Main article read, linked correction body unavailable; effect-size claims excluded. Does not evaluate a laboratory assistant.
sources.implication: Design inference: hint before answering; require a student attempt and evaluate unaided understanding, with faculty review of source and pedagogy.

sources.title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
sources.authors: Greg Kestin, Kelly Miller, Anna Klales, Timothy Milbourne and Gregorio Ponti
sources.locator: Methods, results and limitations; two undergraduate physics lessons, 194 eligible students.
sources.finding: The authors report strong post-test outcomes from a carefully constructed physics tutor compared with in-class active learning in a two-lesson crossover study.
sources.limit: At-home versus classroom conditions, short horizon and expert-designed material. No evidence here for equipment operation, long-term retention or replacing faculty.
sources.implication: Design inference: evaluate a narrowly scoped, source-linked hint experience as a complement to teaching, rather than assuming a general chatbot helps.

sources.title: Shared lab equipment booking — Am I alone?
sources.date: Public thread; displayed relative dates not converted to an exact publication date
sources.locator: Original booking complaint; comments on calendar mistakes, successful calendars and willingness to follow rules.
sources.finding: Accounts conflict: some contributors describe recurring booking problems, while others find shared calendars sufficient. Several distinguish tool usability from following agreed procedures.
sources.limit: Unverified identities, self-selection and possible promotional participation. No prevalence estimate, demographic validation or evidence about our users.
sources.implication: Question-generating evidence only: ask about actual enforcement, handover and exceptions before adding booking complexity.

sources.title: Scheduling Shared Equipment
sources.date: Public thread; displayed relative dates not converted to an exact publication date
sources.locator: Comments on per-equipment calendars, training-based access, paper notes and capacity confusion; promotional comments excluded from recommendations.
sources.finding: Contributors describe different lightweight scheduling practices and confusion about booking equipment capacity and permissions.
sources.limit: Unverified public accounts from varied laboratories, not representative research. Product recommendations and prices in comments are not relied on.
sources.implication: Question-generating evidence only: test whether users understand kit ownership, quantity and permission separately.
